name: Shogun Sugi

location.address: 2242 Iwatani, Mikawa, Aga, Higashikanbara District, Niigata Prefecture (east of Byodo-ji temple)

access: Free, publicly viewable on town-owned land beside Byodo-ji temple.
transport: Rural Aga Town, Niigata Prefecture; reached by car, roughly an hour from Niigata city.
verify_notes: Standalone destination tree and a major superlative claim: at 19.31m trunk girth it was measured as Japan's single largest-girth cedar in the Ministry of the Environment's national giant-tree follow-up survey (FY2000-2001), overtaking Yakushima's Jomon Sugi (16.1m girth), though Jomon Sugi is usually cited as older. Height 38m, estimated age roughly 1,400 years. Name comes from a legend that the Heian-period general Taira no Koremochi spent his later years nearby. Designated National Natural Monument on 8 April 1926 (one source's parenthetical Showa-era date does not match this, so the Aga town official page's Taisho/Showa-15 date of 1926 is used as the more authoritative municipal source). No explicit recent health statement found in the sources fetched, so flagged for that; nothing found suggests decline or death.
